prompts.prompt:
Create a professional brand identity concept for a playful multiplayer browser soapbox racing game called SILICON RACER. Tagline exactly: Big ideas. Bad brakes. This is one cohesive brand identity board, not a website, UI mockup or multiple alternative brands. Target dimensions 1536 x 1024 landscape. Strong hierarchy, exceptional legible typography, generous purposeful whitespace, crisp logo edges, no mock browser chrome, no tiny explanatory paragraphs. The game is a warm humorous SF miniature world: players assemble a sourdough loaf, burrito, crab pot, Victorian porch or driverless pod on wheels and race downhill, hold to charge/release to hop. Startup satire and local SF character. Input image 1 is the existing cityscape reference; image 2 is chassis silhouette reference. They ground the illustrated game world but are not edit targets. Create original artwork in the same broad toy-diorama family, simplify tiny detail. Keep the brand wordmark simple enough to later redraw as vector; illustrations may be dimensional but lettering must stay readable. Preserve blue/coral player identification in any vehicle application. Exact title must be SILICON RACER, singular. No corporate brand logos, no sponsor logos, no glossy photoreal cars. Include only a hero identity with tagline, one useful small-scale icon/monogram application, and one restrained illustrated application with the actual SF soapbox game. All belong to this ONE design direction. No option numbers. No device mockups, no generic unrelated business stationery. Avoid feature inventory, dense cards, cyberpunk neon, microchip clipart, code brackets, gradients on every element, and tech startup landing-page cliches.

Direction: HILL CLIMB ARCADE. Main canvas warm paper cream #FFF2D4. Giant expressive custom italic block wordmark in deep cobalt #2849E8 with small coral #F4624A offset extrusion, occupying upper left 65% in two lines SILICON / RACER, lively forward slant and crisp confident letters, sophisticated contemporary arcade racing identity. Incorporate a single checkered road/finish motif as the underline, subtly rising over an SF hill; keep letters structurally clear. Tagline below in friendly bold sans. Secondary tiny square icon uses the S of the wordmark and the hill/finish motif. Lower right restrained original illustration of a foil-wrapped burrito soapbox racer with four coral/blue wheels and a tiny helmeted driver, taking a hop, with one minimal Golden Gate tower cue and one soft mint cloud. A small dark cobalt application strip at bottom shows the logo in cream. Hero is graphic brand typography; the illustration supports rather than overwhelms. Joyful, competitive, iconic, highly usable as a game title. No realistic logo shadow cast on paper; crisp flat brand graphics contrasted with softly dimensional miniature racer. Do not print the direction's descriptive name.

Direction: PRE-REVENUE RACING. A witty startup-meets-pit-crew brand with highly original graphic composition. Deep aubergine/near-black ink #211D36 background, butter-yellow #FFDD63 bold rounded lowercase wordmark rendering the name as 'silicon racer' (same exact words, singular), no extra words in title. Large stacked typography left aligned, unusual but readable tightened letterforms, a tiny coral racing-number lozenge tucked near the end. Compact simple icon is an abstract steep road with two wheels seen from the side, no circuit motifs. Exact tagline 'Big ideas. Bad brakes.' in cream #F8F3E8, medium size with ample space. Lower section has one horizontal vibrant coral racing decal application using the same lowercase wordmark and restrained checkered edge. Right third original warm isometric toy diorama driverless white pod on comically small skateboard wheels, a small blank cobalt billboard on its rear, one stylized Victorian house ghosted into dark background; tiny blue/coral flag makes it a contestant, no chrome/polished car vibe. Add a small minimal sticker reading 'PUBLIC BETA' near that scene as a natural part of this identity. Flat design system, bold two-color impact with restrained third-color accents. This should look like irreverent indie game branding, immediately recognisable in a thumbnail, not a finance app, not a space game, no screen mockups. Do not print the direction's descriptive name.

Direction: SAN FRANCISCO SOAPBOX CLUB. Editorial brand board in warm cream #F7F0DF with racing vermilion #E65339 and deep forest #163C32, small fog mint #C9DFD0 accents. Large original race-club badge as the main hero left, with a distinctive stepped/hill contour shape rather than a generic circle; central bold slightly condensed slab-inspired lettering SILICON RACER on two lines, beautifully kerned and entirely readable. Combine a subtle stylized Golden Gate bridge tower, a sloping road, and two miniature checkered pennants into one coherent compact badge; no complicated city collage inside logo. Small supporting text inside badge: 'SAN FRANCISCO'. Tagline outside below: 'Big ideas. Bad brakes.' Make it warm and mischievous, contemporary heritage racing identity, expressive graphic mark usable on a tiny phone screen, patches, and cart number plates. On right restrained original cream/coral toy diorama showing a sourdough loaf racer with a tiny helmeted driver, a little uphill street and one Victorian porch/house, simplified enough not to compete with badge. Along bottom one long clean horizontal wordmark application with a racing number 01 at its right, and one small single-color icon version of the hill/bridge mark. Controlled alignment and lots of negative space. Graphics stay crisp and contemporary, avoid distressing, worn paper, fake grain, retro beer label, elaborate heraldry, or tourist souvenir feel. Do not print the direction's descriptive name.
